what: HIGH (code audit CA-A10-200, MEASURED 2026-09-27): scripts/ops/rebuild_pnl_from_bybit_action.sh hardcodes `--apply` on every dispatch of the `rebuild-pnl-from-bybit` Tier-2 system action, with no ACTION_APPLY gate anywhere in the file -- unlike every other Tier-2 money-DB-writing sibling wrapper in scope (mark-operator-flattened, reconcile-netting-rows, repair-netted-rows, repair-malformed-notes, the supersede-* actions, reconcile-orphan-history, fix-prop-mislinked-close, reattach-stranded-package-legs), all of which require an explicit `apply: true` in the issue body before writing and default to a dry-run preview. rebuild_pnl_from_bybit.py's own argparse defines --apply as store_true (default dry-run) -- the python helper is dry-run-safe by design; the bash wrapper is what removes that safety, so every dispatch immediately rewrites the matched rows' pnl/exit_price/pnl_percent/notes for the given account/window with no preview step. The action also has zero row in docs/claude/system-actions.md's §2 allowlist table (only a bare Tier-2 bullet in §3), so this gap was undocumented anywhere a session or the operator would naturally look before dispatching it. Full finding + evidence: docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-A10.findings.jsonl id CA-A10-200. Proposed fix: add the same ACTION_APPLY case-gate every sibling wrapper already uses, and a full §2 table row.
